patch_description:
This redesign replaces the prior Kalman/consensus structure with a robust endpoint local-polynomial tracker combined with a hysteretic directional controller.

For every causal sliding window, the algorithm performs a clipped, exponentially weighted local linear regression whose estimate is evaluated at the newest sample. This retains substantially less phase delay than a moving average while reducing the influence of impulsive samples. Raw window MAD is used only to protect the initial regression from extreme outliers. A separate residual MAD is then calculated after fitting; this distinguishes a clean ramp or curve from genuinely noisy data and controls confidence, smoothing, velocity adaptation, and reversal thresholds.

The fitted endpoint and local slope feed a predictive trend tracker. Unlike a conventional smoother, the tracker requires persistent, noise-significant opposite slope evidence before accepting a directional reversal. During pending reversal evidence, it decelerates toward zero rather than immediately changing sign. This reduces noise-driven trend flips while preserving responsiveness to sustained real reversals.
